ogTitle: Everett Tile Installation — Built From the Membrane Up
ogDesc: Showers and floors for Everett's craftsman-to-split-level housing stock: bonded waterproofing, a photographed 24-hour flood test, and a straight answer on repair versus re-tile. Call (425) 595-1079.

roles.heroLead: The tile you can see was never the waterproofing — the membrane under it does that job. In an Everett house, 1910s craftsman or 90s split-level, that hidden layer decides whether a shower runs twenty years or ends in a $40,000 framing repair. We build the assembly, hold a 24-hour flood test, photograph the result, and only then set tile.
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Everett, WA?
roles.costP1: Figure $14–$26 per square foot installed for tile work in Everett — that spread covers tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor, with labor by itself starting at $11/sq ft. Expect $3,200–$6,800 for a standard tub-shower surround, and somewhere from $6,500 to $14,000 for a complete bathroom with floor, shower and niche.
roles.costP2: Here's the part that surprises people: the shape of the tile moves your bill more than its price tag. A $12 large-format porcelain plank can go in cheaper than a $4 mosaic sheet, because you pay for cuts and grout lines, not for the receipt.
roles.costNote: Everett ranges, installed, as of August 2026 — tile, materials and labor together. The number that counts is the written quote from your free estimate.
roles.layersLead: Seven layers sit between your framing and your grout, and every failed shower we open up in Everett is missing at least one — usually the membrane, skipped to save a few hundred dollars on day one and costing thousands to put right later.
roles.whyP1: Leaks don't knock. Water slips past the grout, wicks into the substrate, and surfaces a couple of winters later as a spongy hallway floor or a brown ring on the ceiling underneath. At that point you're not buying tile anymore — you're buying framing, subfloor, drywall and the whole shower again.
roles.whyP2: Roughly a tenth of what a shower costs is the waterproofing. No line item in a bathroom remodel is more expensive to skip.
roles.scopeIntro: These are starting prices — format, substrate condition and layout push them around. On site we put the real one in writing, free.
roles.cardShower: Pre-slope, bonded membrane, flood test, then niche, curb or curbless entry and tile over it all. What you're really paying for is the part that disappears behind the wall.
roles.cardFloors: Kitchens, baths, entries, mudrooms, basements. We flatten the subfloor first and add an uncoupling membrane wherever movement or radiant heat demands one.
roles.cardBacksplash: Herringbone, subway, mosaic sheet or slab-look porcelain — with clean outlet cuts, finished edge trim, and grout picked to suit the counter rather than the tile carton.
roles.cardHeated: Radiant electric mat on an uncoupling membrane, resistance-checked before and after tile goes down, wired to a dedicated circuit. Makes sense only while the floor is already open.
roles.cardRepair: Loose shower corners, failed grout, cracked field tile. You get a straight answer on whether a repair will hold or the substrate underneath is already gone.
roles.cardDemo: Thinset, backer and old tile out, dust held back with sheeting and negative air, all of it hauled away. Your driveway stays clear.

roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Everett, WA?
roles.faqA1: Expect roughly $14 to $26 per square foot installed for Everett tile work — tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor all counted, with labor alone from $11 per square foot. A standard tub-shower surround comes in at $3,200 to $6,800; plan on $6,500 to $14,000 for a whole bathroom with floor, shower and niche. Format matters more than the tile's price tag: mosaics and large-format both demand noticeably more labor per square foot than a plain 12×12.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Everett?
roles.faqA2: For a standard alcove shower in Everett, budget $3,200 to $6,800 — demolition, a bonded waterproofing system, the sloped pan or base, tile, a niche and grout are all inside that number. Steam showers, benches, curbless entries and full-height stone land higher. Waterproofing takes about a tenth of the total, and it's the piece that heads off the failure measured in tens of thousands.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Always. Behind every shower we set there's a bonded waterproofing system — not bare cement board with thinset over it. The base is pre-sloped, a sheet or liquid membrane runs up the walls, every corner, seam and pipe penetration gets sealed, and a documented 24-hour flood test happens before any tile does. Grout and tile only shed water; the membrane is what actually keeps it out of your framing.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Four to six working days is normal for an Everett bathroom: demolition and dust protection on day one, substrate and waterproofing next with a 24-hour flood test riding on it, a day or two of setting, then grout, silicone and trim to close it out. The shower needs another 24 hours of cure before its first use. A floor by itself usually runs one to two days.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: For anything wet or walked on, porcelain: it's denser, chips less, and absorbs under 0.5% water. Ceramic costs less and does fine work on walls and backsplashes. Our Everett spec is simple — porcelain on every floor and shower floor, ceramic or glass where it only has to look good.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes — and in an Everett winter it earns its keep. An electric radiant mat under tile runs $11 to $16 per square foot installed, thermostat included, and it only pencils out while the floor is already torn up — which is what makes it the cheapest luxury in the house. It sits on an uncoupling membrane, gets resistance-tested before and after the tile, and takes a dedicated circuit.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: In most cases, yes. Demo and haul-away run about $3.50 per square foot, and pulling the old floor is the only honest look you get at the subfloor — rot, movement, past leaks — plus it keeps the new floor height correct at doorways. Going over existing tile can work on a flat, sound, well-bonded surface, but it buries problems we'd rather meet at demo than after grout, and in Everett's older housing stock there's usually something worth finding.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Everett?
roles.faqA8: Plan on $1,100 to $2,200 for a typical Everett backsplash of about 30 square feet, with outlet cuts, edge trim and color-matched grout included. The top of that range belongs to mosaic sheets, herringbone, a framed detail over the range and slab-look porcelain run full height — layout and cutting time is what you're paying for there.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Frequently — and telling you which is which is half our job in Everett. Repair and regrout work starts at $8 per square foot: the right call when grout is stained or crumbling, a dropped pan cracked a tile or two, or shower corners need old grout swapped for silicone. But hollow-sounding tile, tiles releasing in a pattern, or a wall with any give means the substrate has already failed, and a patch only buys months. We say which one you have before the quote, not after.
roles.faqQ10: Which Everett neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: All of Everett is in range — Riverside, Delta, Bayside, Port Gardner, Rucker Hill, Northwest Everett, Lowell, View Ridge-Madison, Evergreen, Glacier View, Pinehurst, Silver Lake, Westmont, Boulevard Bluffs, Cascade View and Holly — along with Marysville, Mukilteo, Lake Stevens, Snohomish, Mill Creek and the rest of Snohomish County down into King County.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: OC Flooring backs tile installation with a 2-year workmanship warranty — double what we offer on carpet, because tile problems surface in year two rather than week two. When we install a manufacturer's complete waterproofing assembly, their system warranty applies on top. We also photograph the membrane and flood test, so the proof travels with the house if you ever sell it.
